long_biography.plain_text:
At Palermo's QuattroPuntoZero, Aloisa Moncada di Paternò has used project management and fundraising to turn endangered craft traditions into training and employment pathways. She directs the distributed arts-and-crafts school, working with social organisations, universities and businesses to rebuild workshops and professional networks in the city's historic centre.

That civic focus followed two terms on the University of Palermo's museum-system council, where Moncada held a special brief for the Botanical Garden. She helped develop restoration projects and new cultural programming. She also served as an ambassador for Manifesta 12. The school's programme includes practical courses, work placements and artisan-led training in Palermo's historic centre.
